chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: Norma leaves him and returns
summary: Cobb says his present wife Norma left on October 6, 1975 after his drinking and arguments, stayed away two years and then phoned to say she missed him.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: When Norma came, she didn't stay away from you then, huh?
Two years. But one morning about 2:00 o'clock she called me, after she got over her mad -- I don't know what the hell she was mad about.
Yeah. She didn't want to speak to me.
You must have been acting very bad.
I must have been doing something.
But she come back, I said, "God damn it, what's on your mind?" She said, "I'm just so lonesome, and I miss you." Yes, she did tell me that. But she didn't know how glad I was to hear that.
But I didn't know what to say to her. I swear to God (inaudible) because I'm a little timid. She's got more guts than I got.
But that's all right. We got guts together now.
Long as there's a happy ending.
Yeah, that's the most important. You see, (inaudible) get ready to walk, October the 6th. I remember the date she walked on me.
See that little girl sitting right there? She said, "Come on, Tina, let's go." Those were her last words -- "Come on, Keemer, let's go."
You don't remember the date I found you.
(Inaudible). You still got that microphone on me?
